note: Dense WORLD historical nodes where the live seed was thin: medieval Europe specifics, a short China dynasty arc, Mongols, WWI/WWII specifics around the existing whole-war nodes, India 1947. Almost all historical. No church-history-as-subject titles. Castle with Many Rooms already shipping covers Charlemagne/Norman/Black Death/Constantinople as family spine—do not re-add it. Books only where a page opened this pass gave age and a clean-enough read for this house.
source: Britannica event pages for years; Common Sense Media, Ignatius Press, Penguin Random House, Kirkus, History Unboxed, Squeaky Clean Reviews for books

events.title: Qin unifies China
events.yearNote: Britannica Qin dynasty: first great Chinese empire, lasting 221–207 BCE; Qin Shi Huang creator of the first unified Chinese empire, reigned 221–210 BCE.
events.summary: The state of Qin conquers the last rival states and forms one Chinese empire under the First Emperor.
context: History, not Scripture. Short, hard dynasty after a long age of warring states.
Later dynasties kept much of the Qin pattern of rule.

events.title: Tang dynasty in China
events.yearNote: Britannica Tang dynasty: 618–907 CE, a cultural and artistic flowering often called a golden age.
events.summary: The Tang dynasty rules China in a long stretch known for strong government, trade, and the arts.
context: One spine stop on a short China arc. Not a theology of China.

events.title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
events.yearNote: Britannica: on Christmas Day of 800, Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne emperor of the Romans. Charlemagne page lists him emperor 800–814.
events.summary: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor in Rome on Christmas Day.
context: Western Europe gains an imperial title after the fall of Rome in the West.
A Castle with Many Rooms (already shipping) treats Charlemagne in its Middle Ages spine.

events.title: Norman Conquest
events.yearNote: Britannica Norman Conquest: decisive victory at Hastings on October 14, 1066; Quick Facts date 1066–1071.
events.summary: William of Normandy defeats Harold at Hastings and takes the English crown.
context: Battle and conquest. Keep the kid summary short; no graphic blow-by-blow.

events.title: Mongol Empire
events.yearNote: Britannica Mongol empire: founded by Genghis Khan in 1206; Quick Facts date 1206–1368; largest contiguous land empire in history.
events.summary: Genghis Khan and his heirs build a vast land empire from East Asia deep into the west.
context: Conquest on a huge scale. Age-gate any book that dwells on cruelty.

events.title: The Black Death
events.yearNote: Britannica Black Death: pandemic that ravaged Europe between 1347 and 1351; Quick Facts date 1347–1351.
events.summary: A great plague sweeps Europe. Many die. Towns and farms are left thin.
context: True and sad. No graphic disease detail in the kid-facing summary.
Magna Carta (1215) already on the map before this node.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.yearNote: Britannica Fall of Constantinople: May 29, 1453; Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II takes the city after a long siege; Byzantine Empire ends.
events.summary: Ottoman forces take Constantinople. The Byzantine Empire ends.
context: Siege and conquest. Keep the summary plain.
Gutenberg's press (already on the map) sits in the same decade.

events.title: Chinese Revolution of 1911
events.yearNote: Britannica Chinese Revolution: October 10, 1911–February 12, 1912; overthrew the Qing dynasty and created a republic.
events.summary: Revolt ends Qing rule and China becomes a republic.
context: Start of a hard modern century in China. Later nodes pick up 1949.

events.title: World War I begins
events.yearNote: Britannica World War I Quick Facts: Date July 28, 1914–November 11, 1918.
events.summary: Austria-Hungary goes to war. The conflict spreads across Europe.
context: Specific start node beside the whole-war card mo-ww1 (already on the map).
Only a Dog and Never Give In already ship for the war as a whole.

events.title: United States enters World War I
events.yearNote: Britannica WWI U.S. entry section: House approved the war resolution on April 6; presidential declaration of war followed immediately.
events.summary: The United States declares war on Germany and joins the Allies.
context: Slots after the whole-war node mo-ww1.

events.title: Treaty of Versailles
events.yearNote: Britannica Treaty of Versailles: signed June 28, 1919, in the Hall of Mirrors; took force January 10, 1920.
events.summary: The Allies and Germany sign the peace treaty that ends World War I on paper.
context: Hard terms on Germany. Later trouble grows from this settlement.

events.title: Germany invades Poland
events.yearNote: Britannica Invasion of Poland: Nazi Germany invaded from September 1 to October 5, 1939; marks the start of World War II.
events.summary: Germany invades Poland. Britain and France go to war. World War II begins in Europe.
context: Specific start node beside the whole-war card mo-ww2 (already on the map).

events.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
events.yearNote: Britannica Pearl Harbor attack: December 7, 1941; Japanese surprise attack on the U.S. naval base in Hawaii.
events.summary: Japan attacks the U.S. fleet at Pearl Harbor. The United States enters World War II.
context: Pacific war opens for America. Keep the summary short; no graphic casualty lists.

events.title: D-Day: Normandy Invasion
events.yearNote: Britannica Normandy Invasion: launched on June 6, 1944 (D-Day); Allied landings on five Normandy beachheads.
events.summary: Allied troops land in Normandy, France, and open a major front in western Europe.
context: Battle day. Age-gate books; no graphic beach detail in the kid summary.

events.title: The Holocaust
events.yearNote: Britannica Holocaust Quick Facts: Date 1933–1945. Systematic state-sponsored killing of six million Jewish people and millions of others by Nazi Germany and collaborators. Placed before the 1939 Poland node because Britannica dates the Holocaust from 1933.
events.summary: Nazi Germany murders millions of Jewish men, women, and children, and many others. It is true. Tell it carefully by age.
context: Atrocity node. Kid-facing summary stays plain. No graphic detail.
Books on this node must be age-gated or previewOnly.

events.title: World War II ends
events.yearNote: Britannica World War II Quick Facts: Date September 3, 1939–September 2, 1945. V-E Day page notes Germany’s surrender celebrated May 8, 1945; the war’s listed end date is September 2, 1945.
events.summary: Fighting ends. Japan’s formal surrender closes the worldwide war.
context: Europe’s victory day came in May; the listed end of the war is September 2.

events.title: Independence and partition of India
events.yearNote: Britannica Partition of India: Indian Independence Act July 18, 1947; took effect August 15, 1947; India and Pakistan become independent amid mass displacement and communal violence.
events.summary: British rule ends. India and Pakistan become independent. Many families must flee.
context: Joy and grief together. Age-gate books that show the violence of partition.

events.title: People’s Republic of China founded
events.yearNote: Britannica Chinese Civil War: Mao proclaimed the People’s Republic of China on October 1, 1949, capital Beijing. Civil War span given as 1945–49.
events.summary: After civil war, Mao Zedong proclaims the People’s Republic of China.
context: Closes this short China arc that began with Qin unification.
Not a devotion book. History of a modern state.

books.title: The Great Wall
books.author: Elizabeth Mann
books.blurb: Picture-heavy Wonders of the World book on why and how China built the wall, and how it failed to keep the north out.
books.parentNote: War and invasion are in the story. Kirkus notes a fold-out of an attack on the wall. Not a cozy picture book for the baby and toddler.

books.title: G is for Genghis Khan
books.author: History Unboxed
books.blurb: Alphabetical picture introduction to Genghis Khan and the Mongol Empire, with adult notes beside simpler kid text.
books.parentNote: Publisher rates it Theme Level 3: moderate violence or conflict themes. Read-aloud so you can skip or explain. Not a graphic war book, but conquest is the subject.

books.title: The Winged Watchman
books.author: Hilda van Stockum
books.blurb: A Dutch family in an old windmill lives under Nazi occupation: hiding, courage, and ordinary family life under pressure.
books.parentNote: Occupation, a hidden Jewish child, a downed RAF pilot, and underground danger. Ignatius lists ages 10 and up. Preview before a mixed-age read-aloud with kids under 10.

books.title: Snow Treasure
books.author: Marie McSwigan
books.blurb: Norwegian children sled gold past Nazi guards to keep their country’s treasure out of enemy hands.
books.parentNote: Danger and arrest risk. Squeaky Clean Reviews: little on-page violence; one character arrested and at risk of execution; brief talk of Nazi brutality in Poland. Penguin age range 8–12.

books.title: Number the Stars
books.author: Lois Lowry
books.blurb: A Danish girl helps her Jewish friend reach safety in Sweden during the Nazi occupation.
books.parentNote: Common Sense Media age 9+: tense meetings with Nazi soldiers, a slap, deaths and disappearances mentioned, a baby given medicine to stay quiet. No sexual content and no profanity on the CSM guide. Not for the youngest listeners.

books.title: Twenty and Ten
books.author: Claire Huchet Bishop
books.blurb: Twenty French schoolchildren and a nun hide ten Jewish refugee children from the Nazis.
books.parentNote: Penguin age range 10 and up. The danger is real: discovery would mean betrayal under Nazi threat. Shorter than Number the Stars; still not a cozy picture book.

books.title: Sadako and the Thousand Paper Cranes
books.author: Eleanor Coerr
books.blurb: True story of Sadako Sasaki of Hiroshima, who folds paper cranes while dying of leukemia years after the atomic bomb.
books.parentNote: Preview only. Common Sense Media age 9+: the girl dies; hospital pain and family grief are vivid; bomb history is named. Japan after the war, not a battle yarn. Not a mixed-age read-aloud.

books.title: The Night Diary
books.author: Veera Hiranandani
books.blurb: A twelve-year-old girl’s diary of flight during the 1947 partition of India and Pakistan.
books.parentNote: Preview only. Common Sense Media age 10+: religious warfare, refugee flight, and a scene where a stranger holds a knife to a tween’s throat. No sexual content and no profanity on the CSM guide. Independent for the older kids after a parent preview.

leftOff.title: Otto of the Silver Hand
leftOff.author: Howard Pyle
leftOff.why: IgniteLit: killing and bloodshed throughout; hand maimed; unfinished as a family read-aloud. Too violent for the default path. No cleaner medieval substitute verified this pass beyond books already shipping (Door in the Wall, Adam of the Road, Castle with Many Rooms).

leftOff.title: The House of Sixty Fathers
leftOff.author: Meindert DeJong
leftOff.why: Plugged In: Japanese invasion of China, burning villages, starvation, bleeding horses, people eating pets; boy prays to a river god. Age listed 8–12 there, but too raw for this house’s default path. No cleaner China-WWII living book cleared this pass.

leftOff.title: Young Fu of the Upper Yangtze
leftOff.author: Elizabeth Foreman Lewis
leftOff.why: Reviews note opium, bandits, political violence, foot-binding references, and dated outsider language. Not cleared as family-clean without a line-by-line parents’ guide. Omitted.

leftOff.title: A Proud Taste for Scarlet and Miniver
leftOff.author: E. L. Konigsburg
leftOff.why: Publisher and review bands lean 10–14 / older middle school; heaven–purgatory framing and mature court politics. Oldest independent reader here is 13; not cleared as a mixed-age default.

leftOff.title: Kubla Khan: The Emperor of Everything
leftOff.author: Kathleen Krull
leftOff.why: Penguin ages 8–12 verified, but reviews note concubines, many wives, and conquest savagery. Left off the default path; G is for Genghis Khan is the simpler Mongol intro used instead.

leftOff.title: Genghis Khan and the Mongol Horde
leftOff.author: Harold Lamb
leftOff.why: Landmark title. IgniteLit warns of Chinese torture description, killings, and a death-cart scene. Too much for default; not used.

leftOff.title: When Hitler Stole Pink Rabbit
leftOff.author: Judith Kerr
leftOff.why: CSM age 9+: suicide by sleeping pills; concentration-camp account of a professor forced to live like a dog; antisemitic slurs. Stronger content than Number the Stars / Twenty and Ten for this house. Left off.

leftOff.title: The Apple and the Arrow
leftOff.author: Mary and Conrad Buff
leftOff.why: HarperCollins vendor page ages 8+; Keenly Kept notes murder, blinding, and wine. No William Tell / Swiss Confederation event added this pass (out of the named gap list), so the book was not slotted.

leftOff.title: Ms. Frizzle's Adventures: Imperial China
leftOff.author: Joanna Cole
leftOff.why: Could not open a page this pass that both confirmed a clean age band for this specific title and cleared deep-time / science-series assumptions. Magic School Bus CSM is science-framed. Omitted rather than guess.

leftOff.title: Han dynasty / Song dynasty / Qing dynasty / Meiji Japan / Cold War start as its own node
leftOff.why: China arc kept to Qin, Tang, 1911, and 1949 so the chunk stays one coherent pass. Meiji and a separate Cold War start were skipped; Berlin Wall already covers a Cold War hinge. Ming was verified (Britannica 1368–1644) but left out to stay near the event cap—can be a later pass.
